summary: Iteration 8 backup module fully tested: 10/10 PASS in test_iter8_backups.py. Full regression (iter5+iter6+iter7+iter8) = 58/58 PASS when run serially. Verified: POST /api/backups admin creates snapshot with proper filename pattern (liniar-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json), size>0, counts for all 5 collections, total_rows=sum(counts), ISO created_at, created_by=admin email; POST without auth -> 401; staff -> 403. GET /api/backups admin lists descending by created_at; staff -> 403. GET /api/backups/{id}/download returns application/json with Content-Disposition attachment containing filename, JSON body has generated_at + app='liniar' + collections{purchases, production, sales_transactions, inventory, operating_expenses}. Downloaded row counts exactly match metadata counts. FORBIDDEN collections (users, activity_logs) confirmed absent from JSON payload. Non-existent id -> 404, staff download -> 403. activity_logs entry with entity=backup, action=create, entity_id matching, summary contains filename and total_rows. Object-storage round-trip works via Emergent Object Storage proxy (put_object + get_object).

minor.issue: Running iter5-8 with parallel xdist (addopts -n 2 --dist loadscope) causes iter5 OpEx tests to error and iter7 pagination to fail due to session/global state sharing across workers. Serial (-n 0) is 100% green. Pre-existing infra concern, not an iter8 regression.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to 537 lines with backup endpoints inlined. Splitting into routers (auth, purchases, production, sales, opex, reports, activity_logs, backups) is now overdue.

backup endpoint calls asyncio.to_thread(put_object) which uses a single global _storage_key. init_storage() has no re-init on 401/expired-key path — if the storage key expires mid-runtime, backups will fail permanently until restart. Consider catching auth errors and re-initializing.
storage.py uses synchronous `requests` inside asyncio.to_thread. For large backups, this blocks a thread for full upload duration. Acceptable for MVP but flag for aiohttp/httpx-async in scale.

Backup payload uses json.dumps(default=str) — datetime and ObjectId become strings; downstream restore code will need matching parsing. Recommend Bson-safe extended-json format if restore is ever implemented.
backups collection has no index on created_at; list endpoint sorts on it. Add index in seed_data().
download endpoint streams entire body into memory via Response(content=data). For multi-MB backups this is fine, but consider StreamingResponse if snapshot grows past ~50MB.
No delete/retention endpoint for backups — history will grow unbounded in Mongo + object storage. Add TTL/retention policy (e.g., keep last N or last 30 days).
seed_data_creation: 1 real backup snapshot created and uploaded to Emergent Object Storage during test run (liniar-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json). Adds one row to db.backups and one entry to activity_logs (entity=backup).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backup endpoints: POST /api/backups (admin), GET /api/backups (admin), GET /api/backups/{id}/download (admin). All wired to Emergent Object Storage via INTEGRATION_PROXY_URL + EMERGENT_LLM_KEY (storage.py). Object-storage calls latency 1-3s per put/get in this env — actual test finished in 2.6s so timeouts are fine at 30-120s. BACKUP_COLLECTIONS = purchases, production, sales_transactions, inventory, operating_expenses. Users/activity_logs deliberately excluded. When running full regression, use `pytest -n 0` (serial) to avoid iter5/iter7 flakes from cross-worker state sharing.
